'''''Phaseolus''''' ('''bean''', '''wild bean''')<ref>{{ITIS |id=203844 |taxon=''Phaseolus''}}</ref> is a [[genus]] of herbaceous to woody annual and perennial vines in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Fabaceae]] containing about 70 [[plant]] [[species]], all native to the [[Americas]], primarily [[Mesoamerica]].<ref name=":0">{{cite journal | last1 = Delgado-Salinas |first1=A. |last2=Thulin |first2=M. |last3=Pasquet |first3=R. |last4=Weeden |first4=N. |last5=Lavin |first5=M. | year = 2011 | title = ''Vigna'' (Leguminosae) ''sensu lato'': the names and identities of the American segregate genera | journal = [[American Journal of Botany]] | volume = 98 | issue = 10 | pages = 1694–715 | doi = 10.3732/ajb.1100069 | pmid = 21980163}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Taxonomy, distribution, and ecology of the genus Phaseolus (Leguminosae-Papilionoideae) in North America, Mexico and Central America|last1=Freytag|first1=George F.|last2=Debouck|first2=Daniel G.|date=2002|publisher=Botanical Research Institute of Texas|isbn=1889878111|oclc=249436749}}</ref>

It is one of the most economically important legume genera. Five of the species have been [[domestication|domesticated]] since [[pre-Columbian]] times for their [[bean]]s: ''[[Phaseolus acutifolius|P. acutifolius]]'' (tepary bean), ''[[Phaseolus coccineus|P. coccineus]]'' (runner bean), ''[[Phaseolus dumosus|P. dumosus]]'' (year bean), ''[[Phaseolus lunatus|P. lunatus]]'' (lima bean), and ''[[Phaseolus vulgaris|P. vulgaris]]'' (common bean).<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Rosales-Serna | first1 = R. | last2 = Hernández-Delgado | first2 = S. | last3 = González-Paz | first3 = M. | last4 = Acosta-Gallegos | first4 = J. A. | last5 = Mayek-Pérez | first5 = N. | title = Genetic Relationships and Diversity Revealed by AFLP Markers in Mexican Common Bean Bred Cultivars | doi = 10.2135/cropsci2004.0582 | journal = Crop Science | volume = 45 | issue = 5 | pages = 1951 | year = 2005 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bitocchi|first1=Elena|last2=Rau|first2=Domenico|last3=Bellucci|first3=Elisa|last4=Rodriguez|first4=Monica|last5=Murgia|first5=Maria L.|last6=Gioia|first6=Tania|last7=Santo|first7=Debora|last8=Nanni|first8=Laura|last9=Attene|first9=Giovanna|date=2017-05-08|title=Beans (Phaseolus ssp.) as a Model for Understanding Crop Evolution|journal=Frontiers in Plant Science|volume=8|page=722|doi=10.3389/fpls.2017.00722|pmid=28533789|pmc=5420584|issn=1664-462X|doi-access=free}}</ref> Most prominent among these is the [[common bean]], ''P. vulgaris'', which today is cultivated worldwide in tropical, semitropical, and temperate [[climate]]s.

== Ecology ==
''Phaseolus'' species are used as food plants by the [[larva]]e of some [[Lepidoptera]] species, including [[Common Swift (moth)|common swift]], [[garden dart]], [[ghost moth]] ''[[Hypercompe albicornis]]'', ''[[Hypercompe icasia|H. icasia]]'' and the [[Nutmeg (moth)|nutmeg]].

== Taxonomy ==

The generic name ''Phaseolus'' was introduced by [[Carl Linnaeus|Linnaeus]] in 1753,<ref name="linnaeus">Linnaeus, ''[[Species Plantarum]]'' '''2''':623, cited in [[Oxford English Dictionary]] [http://oed.com/view/Entry/142272 ''s.v.'' 'phaseolus']</ref> from the [[Latin language|Latin]] ''phaseolus'', a [[diminutive]] of ''phasēlus'', in turn borrowed from [[Greek language|Greek]] {{lang|el|φάσηλος}} ''phasēlos'' used for either a species labelled as ''[[Cowpea|Vigna sinensis]]'', or "calavance" which is an old name for the [[chickpea#Etymology|chickpea]]; that word itself is of unknown origin.<ref name="oed">[[Oxford English Dictionary]] [http://oed.com/view/Entry/142272 ''s.v.'' 'phaseolin']</ref><ref>{{LSJ|fa/shlos|φάσηλος|ref}}</ref> The Ancient Greeks probably referred to any bean in a pod as ''phasēlos'' including those species, [[mung bean]] as well as [[Vigna mungo|black gram]] which were brought to them from Asia during their time; the name extended to the New World beans with the introduction of [[common bean]] into Europe via [[Columbian exchange]] in the 16th century and later given the name ''Phaseolus vulgaris''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Heinrich |first1= F. B. J. |last2=Wilkins |first2=D. A. |year=2014 |title=Beans, boats and archaeobotany: A new translation of 'phasolus' or why the romans ate neither kidney beans nor cowpeas |url=https://ugp.rug.nl/Palaeohistoria/article/view/24926/22374 |journal=Palaeohistoria |volume=55/56 |issue=2013/2014 |pages=149–176 |s2cid=58931881}}</ref>

Previous classifications placed a number of other well-known [[legume]] species in this genus, but they were subsequently reassigned to the genus ''[[Vigna]]'', sometimes necessitating a change of species name. For example, older literature refers to the [[mung bean]] as ''Phaseolus aureus'', whereas more modern sources classify it as ''Vigna radiata''. Similarly, the snail bean ''[[Vigna caracalla]]''  was discovered in 1753 and in 1970 moved from ''Phaseolus'' to ''Vigna''. The modern understanding of ''Phaseolus'' indicates a genus [[endemism|endemic]] only to the New World.<ref name=":0" />

==Allergenicity==
The ''Phaseolus'' plant has an [[OPALS (Ogren Plant Allergy Scale)|OPALS plant allergy scale]] rating of 4 out of 10, indicating moderate potential to cause allergic reactions, exacerbated by over-use of the same plant throughout a garden. Leaves can cause skin rash and old plants often carry [[Rust (fungus)|rust]].<ref name = "Ogren">{{cite book|last=Ogren|first=Thomas Leo|title=The Allergy-Fighting Garden|date=2015|publisher=Ten Speed Press|location=Berkeley|isbn=9781607744917}}</ref>
